status: preimplementation independent plan; every case unexecuted
ownership: No product files, evaluator scripts or product-generated expected fixtures are supplied. All coordinates/formulas are original independent recipes.
root_scope_decision: First integrated phase is actual authored material-outline offset, not cutting-guide-only allowance.

global_assumptions.three_d: Y-up; preserve selected piece arrangement, compare intrinsic rest geometry before any deformed-state export
global_assumptions.surface_mass: 0.2 kg/m2, mapped without rounding to the existing material model; if represented as density*thickness, freeze both inputs giving that same areal mass
global_assumptions.default_width: not inferred from MD; every scenario supplies its width
global_assumptions.stable_ids: Record actual IDs after original authoring; do not invent product ID allocation values. Test equality/preservation/remapping against recorded input IDs.

fixtures.attachments: none; no holes; preserve fabric and arrangement

fixtures.same_as: F-CURVE except the right cubic is replaced by these exact de Casteljau halves

fixtures.negative_purpose: An outward distance 0.11 crosses nonadjacent offset source spans across the 0.2-wide notch; phase one must not silently merge them.
Cubic derivative vanishes at t=0.5, point (0.1,0.3).
fixtures.if_source_validation_refuses: Record that refusal separately; do not count it as reaching the offset command. The offset-planner singular-tangent case remains required.

fixtures.relationship: Sew first piece right boundary to second piece left boundary; record the real globally stable owner/curve/sewing IDs. Also prepare an ordered-group variant.
fixtures.negative_purpose: Phase-one attached relationship refusal; no guessed remapping.

fixtures.segments: regular polygon, no zero-length edges or attachments
fixtures.negative_purpose: 4097 valid authored segments exceed the proposed offset-request ceiling independently of document load limits.

expected.representation: One or more ordinary editable authored cubics approximate the curved locus. Rest/display/export tessellation is a separate product.
expected.split_invariance: Offset F-CURVE and F-CURVE-SPLIT agree geometrically within twice fit tolerance; no artificial corner at t=0.5.

expected.fit_certification: A bound between sampling sites is required; the three listed samples and aggregate area alone do not certify global offset error.

oracle.cross_check: A separate dense shoelace integration of the analytic normal locus gave 0.29061134446289494; no WeftForge input or output was used.

expected.rest: Triangulation contains the L domain and excludes the notch; sum of triangle areas matches expected area.

scenarios.title: Unsupported holes and attached sewing refuse without lost data

action.targets: Hole-bearing piece; then sewn piece A with seam variant and ordered sewing-group variant; also any attached internal/pin/tack/link relationship not supported by the reviewed command.

expected.result: Explicit atomic unsupported-relationship/hole refusal identifying the blocker.
expected.identity: Both pieces, all boundary and seam/group IDs, intervals, original settings, document revision/history, current rest/simulation and saved files unchanged.
expected.forbidden: No dropped seam, guessed nearest-edge remap, hole fill, or partial offset of only the exterior.

scenarios.title: Native end-to-end material offset and editable saved result

workflow: Start an empty original project; author the declared fixtures through native controls; save before.
Select rectangle; enter 1 cm Extend; inspect preview dimensions/area/mass; Cancel. Saved/applied state must remain before.
Preview and Apply 10 mm once; save; inspect actual new rest domain/mass. Undo once restores original; Redo once reapplies.
Keep a focused distance draft and cancel it; confirm no accidental Apply on unrelated selection/quit path.
Offset curve and L through native tools; verify their declared numeric outcomes.
Save; close process after retaining outputs; reopen the same project; select and edit a resulting cubic control, then Undo.
Export current material boundary SVG/DXF and the available supported rest-mesh OBJ, retaining success/unsupported outcomes honestly.
Attempt to offset an attached-seam piece; verify explicit refusal and preservation.
Retain screenshots/AX where available plus saved authored geometry, numeric rest/mass records, exports and cleanup record; close finished test windows.

expected.transactions: Every Apply is one undo step; preview/Cancel has no committed revision/ID/history effect.
expected.persistence: Saved/reopened ordinary editable line/cubic geometry, identities, fabric/physical settings and arrangement agree; no new live width attribute is implied.
expected.scale: Applied rectangle physical bounds 420x620 mm; SVG physical dimensions and coordinates agree within 0.01 mm. Supported DXF declares millimetres and has the same material extents. Rest OBJ intrinsic bounds are 0.42x0.62 m after its explicit unit conversion.
expected.mass: Rectangle applied rest area 0.2604 m2 and physical mass 0.05208 kg; old rectangle 0.24 m2/0.048 kg is not used by the current solver.
expected.export_failure: Any genuinely unsupported format/role is explicit and does not replace an existing destination; do not grade unsupported output as success.
expected.evidence: Source and executable identities, initial settings, original recipes, action trace, measurements and cleanup pinned before acceptance; native visual presence alone is insufficient.
expected.mandatory_output_gates: SVG, supported boundary DXF and rest-geometry OBJ for accepted first-phase fixtures must succeed with the stated scale/geometry. An unsupported outcome remains incomplete, not a waiver.

scenarios.title: Hole side semantics and material-area accounting

expected.orientation: Reversing source parameter order does not reverse material-relative side.
expected.relationships: Hole identities/ownership persist; no material added across the hole by triangulation.
expected.phase_one: Must refuse this unsupported input atomically; this numeric result does not constitute phase-one support.

scenarios.title: Persistent seam allowance and relationship behavior remains required

action.role: explicit cutting-guide allowance first; explicit material application separately
future_operations: multiple offsets from previous or selected source

expected.guide_only: Rectangle guide cut bounds 420x620 mm while actual cloth remains 0.24 m2 and 0.048 kg; UI/export identify the guide role.
expected.material_application: Only an explicit material operation changes domain/mass to 0.2604 m2/0.05208 kg.
expected.authority: Settings and stable source references remain authoritative; derived contours are revision-tagged caches, not replacement construction.
expected.relationships: No dropped settings, inferred seam/cut role switch, averaged unequal widths or dangling IDs; new-cut-edge policy must be reviewed before implementation.
expected.phase_one: No persistent-guide model or completion claim is required/earned by material-outline offset.

scenarios.title: Shared-command equivalence, transforms and source edits

action.commands: Same whole-piece material-offset semantics, finite SI width and direction; use independent copies with identical starting authoring and ID counters.
variants: translate source by (1.2,-0.3) m then offset
mirror source, normalizing material side without using incidental winding
uniform/nonuniform resize source first, then offset by the same 0.01 m
split the cubic exactly at t=0.5 before offset

expected.result: All routes produce equivalent ordinary authored geometry, stable-identity rules, actual rest/mass, transaction count and errors.
expected.covariance: Offset commutes with rigid transforms; intrinsic area/mass unchanged by them. Offset after nonuniform resize is a new constant-distance offset, not an affine transform of a prior offset.
expected.resize_exact_subcase: Resize F-RECT to 0.8x0.3 m before 0.01 m Extend: material rectangle 0.82x0.32 m, area 0.2624 m2, mass 0.05248 kg.
expected.saved_result_edit: After Apply, later point/curve edits operate on the resulting ordinary construction; do not pretend an earlier offset width is a persistent parameter.
expected.schemas: CLI help/MCP tool schema and command errors expose the same supported scope.

scenarios.title: Failed load, save and export never replace good data

attempts: Open a malformed project with duplicate global IDs, dangling curve refs, nonfinite coordinates, unknown schema or invalid curve/domain geometry.
Save or export the valid applied project to a destination with a real controlled write failure or cancel before replacement; retain a prior sentinel file and its digest.
Export a curved result through an incapable requested format/role.

expected.load: Open document, authoring/revision/history and current successful saved file remain intact.
expected.write: Existing destination bytes remain exactly the prior digest on failure/cancellation; no success notification or partial file replacing it.
expected.portable: A successful offset result saves/reopens in the current ordinary geometry schema; supported older files still open unchanged.
expected.truth: Record unavailable I/O failure mechanisms or unsupported exporters as blocked/unsupported; do not invent a passing failure injection.

scenarios.title: Bounded preview cancellation and stale-result suppression

attempts: Start offset preview for a valid 4096-segment source; cancel it or change selection/document revision before worker result publication.
Exercise a pre-cancelled token and a cancellation during bounded geometry operations through the existing job/test mechanism.
Exercise output-fit/subdivision/derived-vertex exhaustion when a declared original fixture reaches it; if it cannot be reached, preserve that untested limit explicitly.

expected.limits: <=4096 source segments, <=65536 authored output segments, <=65536 derived vertices, depth <=24; no partial/truncated geometry.
expected.cancellation: Observed at least every 256 geometry operations; no result publishes for an old revision or cancelled request.
expected.authoring: Preview is transient; no permanent IDs/revision/history/file change before successful Apply.
expected.native: Escape cancels the draft even if computation finishes first. A completed-before-cancel run is not counted as a cancelled-worker observation.
expected.offline: Core command/planner requires no GUI or network dependency.
expected.timing: Freeze hardware and record wall-clock UI responsiveness separately; no baseline speed parity inferred.

error_classification_note: Descriptive proposed classifications; final public error names follow existing command conventions.
reference_expectation: Unknown for all cases; these are independent WeftForge engineering requirements, not baseline expectations.
